reason: The text depicts Moses as the primary leader with Aaron serving as his subordinate spokesperson. Although Aaron is identified as a Levite (הַלֵּוִ֔י), the passage explicitly establishes a hierarchy where Moses holds the superior position. God states that Aaron 'shall be your mouth and you shall be to him as God' (וְהָ֤יָה הוּא֙ יִֽהְיֶה־ לְּךָ֣ לְפֶ֔ה וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶה־ לּ֥וֹ לֵֽאלֹהִֽים), establishing that the non-priest Moses is superior to the Levite Aaron in the leadership structure. This directly contradicts the statement's claim of priest superiority.
